# Nordsjælland Børne- og Ungeafdeling

Nordsjælland Børne- og Ungeafdeling is a pediatric and adolescent department participating in the DANIBD (Danish IBD) registry, a national quality monitoring system for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) care across Danish hospitals and regions. The department's performance is tracked against standardized diagnostic indicators that measure the quality and completeness of IBD investigations in children and young people.

As of the 2024 DANIBD audit cycle, Nordsjælland Børne- og Ungeafdeling achieved 56% compliance with indicator 1b, which measures complete IBD diagnostic workup in pediatric patients [^src1]. Complete diagnostic workup for children and young people requires three procedures: gastroscopy, colonoscopy, and either MR scanning or capsule endoscopy. This compliance rate reflects regional and departmental variation seen across Danish hospitals; nationally, only 69% of newly diagnosed pediatric IBD patients meet the complete diagnostic standard, against a development target of 79% that has been achieved for adult colonoscopy screening under indicator 1a [^src1]. The DANIBD registry uses these performance metrics to identify gaps in diagnostic rigor and to inform quality improvement planning, with the next audit evaluation of this indicator scheduled for 2026 [^src1].

- **Three facts with sources**: (1) The department achieved 56% compliance with indicator 1b [^src1]; (2) Indicator 1b measures complete IBD diagnostic workup including gastroscopy, colonoscopy, and MR scanning or capsule endoscopy [^src1]; (3) The national development target for this indicator is 79%, with only 69% national compliance as of 2024 [^src1].
- **Two related entities**: The DANIBD registry (the national quality monitoring system) and regional/departmental hospital networks across Denmark that participate in this monitoring.
